einzeiler: A 12th-century English legend about a young farm worker who suddenly gains the ability…
kurzfassung: A 12th-century chronicle tells the eerie story of a young English farm worker named Kettle whose life changes forever after his horse trips over invisible spirits. He develops the ability to see demons everywhere and adopts a strict, ascetic lifestyle to protect himself. When he forgets to make the protective sign of the cross one night, he is paralyzed by malicious entities before being rescued by a mysterious figure.
stichpunkte: A 12th-century account from Chronicon Anglicanum documents the story of a young farm worker named Kettle.
Kettle's horse trips over invisible entities on a flat road, opening his spiritual eyes to the unseen world.
He discovers that low-level demons are everywhere, whispering, plotting, and causing petty mischief.
To protect himself, Kettle keeps his gift secret, avoids meat, wears rough clothing, and spends all his time at the local church.
He confronts a group of ten demons attempting to terrorize the village, successfully driving them away in the name of Christ.
Exhausted after a long day in the fields, Kettle forgets to make the sign of the cross before falling asleep.
Two demons paralyze and mock him in his bed, seeking revenge for his interference.
A radiant young man holding a battle-axe taps the metal blade, and the resulting vibration terrifies the demons into fleeing.
The mysterious figure warns Kettle that his carelessness almost cost him his life, leaving him to live out his days in watchful faith.

clips.hook: Why did Kettle keep his terrifying ability a strict secret?
clips.text: Kettle chooses not to brag about his supernatural sixth sense, discussing it only with his priest under confession, his master, or deeply sincere questioners to avoid unwanted attention and suspicion.

clips.hook: Ten supernatural figures march into the sleeping village
clips.text: Ten non-human entities march into the village, led by a taller, broader boss possessing an aggressive sense of authority while Kettle watches unseen from a doorway.

clips.hook: Demons frozen in rage by a simple country servant
clips.text: The lead demon's arrogant expression turns to shock and fury because the spoken name of Christ acts as an impenetrable wall and blows their cover.

clips.hook: Trapped and paralyzed inside his own body
clips.text: Kettle tries to make the traditional protective gesture and cry out, but the entities completely bind his hands and tongue, leaving him defenseless.

beschreibung:
This is a lesser-known, short eerie legend of Ketell, as found on Chronicon Anglicanum by Radulphi de Coggeshall. You might recognize the chronicle's name because it's the same one where the story of the Green Children of Woolpit appears.
In this story, an innocent teenager that works the fields has an encounter with small demons that are planning to scare everybody in town. He soon realizes that he's the only one that can see demons and decides to keep the secret for himself. This story reached Radulphi's ears and he documented in the book as a true account. But how terrifying is it to be able to see these evil spirits?
